newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slip despite active cement trade. [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slip despite active cement trade. [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell on Monday (corrects day from Sunday) despite active trade in cement stocks that took the volume to an above-average level, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index closed 0.66 points lower at 234.37 points on volume of 27.31 million pounds ($8.03 million).
"There was very heavy trading in cement stocks which are our black horses," said Neveen el-Tahry of Delta EAB Stockbrokers. "All cement prices were up today. Otherwise, trading was quite low."
Suez Cement lead the cement pack, rising 0.60 pounds to close at 47.85. Shares worth 6.37 million pounds were traded.

Amriyah Cement closed 1.00 pound higher at 60.00 after shares worth nearly five million pounds exchanged hands while Egyptian Tora Portland Cement jumped 2.10 pounds to 62.60 after trading in more than 1.8 million pounds.
Central Egypt Flour Mills was another strong performer, trading in shares worth more than 700,000 pounds but it slipped 0.15 pounds to close at 28.75.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 352.43 points from Sunday's 348.70 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 160.28 from 160.75 points.
